text:
maria: Heads up — seeing high packet loss between pods in gpu-pool during nightly training. Jobs failing to rendezvous, NCCL timeouts. :frowning:

jonathan: Any recent infra changes? networking / netpol deploys?

maria: Not that I'm aware of. I ran a quick iperf between two training pods and got ~40% packet loss. ping also shows intermittent timeouts.

choi: Can you paste the iperf output + kubectl get netpol -n gpu-workloads?

maria: iperf3 output:
```
iperf3 -c 10.0.3.12 -p 50051
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  1.25 GBytes  1.07 Gbits/sec  40.3% packet loss
```
kubectl get netpol -n gpu-workloads -o wide
```
NAME                       POD-SELECTOR            AGE
deny-egress-default        app=deny-default        6d
allow-control-egress       role=control            2d
```

jonathan: That deny-egress-default looks suspicious. Can you describe it?

maria: kubectl get netpol deny-egress-default -n gpu-workloads -o yaml
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-default
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: deny-default
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

choi: Yikes, that's an allow-only list for 80/443/53 — everything else is implicitly denied. That will block ephemeral ports, nodeport traffic, and any custom ports used for RPC/rdma.

pat: NCCL uses range-ish ephemeral ports for rendezvous (and we use gRPC on 50051 for our rendezvous + heartbeat). If egress default only allows 80/443/53 then pod-to-pod on high ports is blocked.

jonathan: That explains the packet loss and failed rendezvous. Two options: (1) broaden the policy to allow pod-to-pod within the same namespace (namespaceSelector) and the nodeport/ephemeral port ranges; or (2) add an explicit allow for the control plane/hosts that need it. Quickfix idea: allow tcp:50051-50070 and the nodePort range 30000-32767.

maria: I can test a temp policy to allow namespace traffic. Applying this now (dry-run first):
```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-intra-gpu-traffic-temp
  namespace: gpu-workloads
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  - Ingress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: gpu-workloads
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50051
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50052
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50053
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50054
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50055
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50056
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50057
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50058
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50059
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 50060
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 30000
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 32767
EOF
```

choi: After apply, run a quick curl/gRPC check between pods and iperf again.

maria: Re-ran iperf3 after applying temp policy:
```
iperf3 -c 10.0.3.12 -p 50051
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  9.86 GBytes  8.46 Gbits/sec   0.2% packet loss
```
Connectivity looks stable now. :tada:

eng-infra-oncall: Created incident INC-20250312-3 for tracking. Please attach the final policy + postmortem.

pat: We should not leave a permissive namespaceSelector forever. Plan: update deny-egress-default to explicitly allow intra-namespace pod CIDR and the known rendezvous ports (50051-50060), and add an annotation that documents why those ports are needed. Also add a network policy unit test in CI that runs a basic pod-to-pod check.

jonathan: +1. Also add an alarm if packet loss > 5% on inter-pod check between gpu nodes. Could be useful for future regressions.

maria: I'll open a PR with the tightened policy and tests, link incident, and roll out during low usage window. Leaving temp policy in place until approved. Thanks for quick triage everyone. :heart:

sre-bot: Incident INC-20250312-3 created and assigned to eng-infra-oncall.
